title: Detecting a GPU and falling back

questions.stem: A service on a laptop with no GPU loads the CUDA build of highspy and sets solver="pdlp" inside a try/except that falls back to interior point. What happens when it runs?

options.text: HiGHS runs PDLP on the CPU instead, a little slower
options.says: The CUDA build's PDLP has no CPU path: without a GPU it kills the process instead of switching to the CPU.

options.text: HiGHS raises an error, and the except runs interior point
options.says: No Python exception is raised: the process is killed by a segmentation fault, so the except never runs.

options.text: The process is killed, and the except clause never runs
options.says: Right: it prints a CUDA context error and dies with SIGSEGV, which is why the check comes before the option is set.

options.text: HiGHS returns the status Unknown, and the service moves on
options.says: There is no status to read: the process is gone before run() returns.

origin.section: Never Ask highspy for PDLP Without a GPU

questions.stem: A new teammate proposes importing cuOpt directly in the planning service, to save the cost of starting a worker process. Which fact about the course's setup rules that out?

options.text: Its log must reach the console, which only a worker can do
options.says: The worker keeps cuOpt's log off the console on purpose, since its header names the card's UUID.

options.text: Its PDLP runs only on a machine where no GPU is found
options.says: cuOpt needs a GPU: run_cuopt refuses to start without one.

options.text: Its solver cannot share a machine with HiGHS at any time
options.says: cuOpt shares the machine, the GPU image and the card with HiGHS; lesson 11.4.3 runs both on the same GPU. Only the environment and the process are kept apart.

options.text: Its data library needs pandas and numpy older than the course's
options.says: Right: cuDF needs older pandas and numpy than the course pins, so the two cannot share one environment, and cuOpt has its own environment and interpreter.

origin.section: cuOpt Runs in a Process of Its Own

questions.stem: On a GPU machine, HiGHS's GPU PDLP returns the status Unknown for a portfolio LP, although its objective is within 3e-8 of the optimum. What should the service do with this answer?

options.text: Use it, since its objective is already within 3e-8
options.says: HiGHS did not stand behind it: its prices broke dual rows by up to 1,100, and the service never uses a result that is not Optimal.

options.text: Solve the LP on the CPU and use that answer instead
options.says: Right: a GPU answer that is not Optimal is the second fallback trigger; the CPU interior point solved GridCap's LP.

options.text: Report the LP as infeasible, since no optimum was found
options.says: Unknown is not infeasible: the CPU fallback solved the same LP to Optimal.

options.text: Use it if its plan keeps every row to within 1e-7
options.says: The plan kept its rows to 9.2e-8 and HiGHS still refused it, because the prices were far from feasible.

origin.section: Fall Back When the GPU Is Missing or Its Answer Is Not Optimal
